title: Nature, the self, and the one who sees

verses.sa: बहिरन्तश्च भूतानामचरं चरमेव च । सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थं चान्तिके च तत् ॥
verses.tr: The supreme reality is inside and outside all beings, moving and unmoving. Because it is subtle, it cannot be known; it is far away and near at hand.
verses.angle: Bahi and antah, outside and inside
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna just said the supreme reality is beyond the senses, yet Krishna now says it is inside and outside all beings.

body.text: The supreme reality is inside and outside all beings, moving and unmoving. Because it is subtle, it cannot be known; it is far away and near at hand. Listen to the word bahi, outside, and antah, inside. It fills everything, yet because it is so subtle, it cannot be known, and it is far away and near at the same time. Krishna now says this undivided reality appears divided among all beings, and that it creates and devours them.

verses.sa: अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम् । भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च ॥
verses.tr: Undivided among beings, it appears divided. Know it as the one who bears, devours, and creates all beings.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: If the supreme reality is everywhere, how does it appear as many? This verse answers that exact question.

body.text: Undivided among beings, it appears divided. Know it as the one who bears, devours, and creates all beings. The verse opens with a paradox: the reality is undivided, yet it appears divided among beings. It is one reality playing the roles of creator, sustainer, and destroyer of all. Krishna now tells us that this reality is the light of all lights, beyond all darkness.

verses.sa: ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते । ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य विष्ठितम् ॥
verses.tr: It is the light of all lights, beyond darkness. It is knowledge, the knowable, reached through knowledge, and abiding in every heart.
verses.angle: Jnanagamyam: the known and the knower are one
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna sets the scene by describing the ultimate reality as the source of all light.

body.text: It is the light of all lights, beyond darkness. It is knowledge, the knowable, reached through knowledge, and abiding in every heart. The word jnanagamyam means reached through knowledge, and here it is knowledge itself. The knower and the known are one and the same. Krishna then briefly summarizes the field, knowledge, and the knowable before telling his devotee about attaining his state.

verses.sa: इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः । मद्भक्त एतद्विज्ञाय मद्भावायोपपद्यते ॥
verses.tr: Thus, field, knowledge, and the knowable have been explained briefly. My devotee, understanding this, attains my state.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now gathers the three terms he has taught, field, knowledge, and the knowable. Listen for the one word that names the reward.

body.text: Thus, field, knowledge, and the knowable have been explained briefly. My devotee, understanding this, attains my state. The word is madbhavaya, to my state. Krishna says that a devotee who understands these three truths reaches his own state, the goal of the entire teaching. Krishna now asks to know Prakriti and Purusha as beginningless, and to see qualities arise from Prakriti.

verses.sa: प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव विद्ध्यनादी उभावपि । विकारांश्च गुणांश्चैव विद्धि प्रकृतिसंभवान् ॥
verses.tr: Know both Prakriti and Purusha to be beginningless, and know the modifications and qualities to arise from Prakriti.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just finished describing the field and the knower. Now he tells Arjuna how to separate the silent witness from the changing world.

body.text: Know both Prakriti and Purusha to be beginningless, and know the modifications and qualities to arise from Prakriti. Krishna names two beginningless realities, Prakriti and Purusha, and says that every modification and quality comes only from Prakriti, leaving the Purusha untouched. He now assigns Prakriti as the cause of the body and action, and the Purusha as the cause of feeling pleasure and pain.

verses.sa: कार्यकारणकर्तृत्वे हेतुः प्रकृतिरुच्यते । पुरुषः सुखदुःखानां भोक्तृत्वे हेतुरुच्यते ॥
verses.tr: Nature is said to be the cause of the body, the senses, and action. The inner being is said to be the cause of experiencing pleasure and pain.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues his explanation of the field and the knower of the field by separating the doer from the experiencer.

body.text: Nature is said to be the cause of the body, the senses, and action. The inner being is said to be the cause of experiencing pleasure and pain. Prakriti causes the body, senses and action, Krishna says, while Purusha is the cause of experiencing pleasure and pain. Krishna then explains that the inner being, situated in nature, experiences the qualities born of nature.

verses.sa: पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्क्ते प्रकृतिजान्गुणान् । कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु ॥
verses.tr: The inner being, situated in nature, experiences the qualities born of nature. Attachment to those qualities causes birth in good and bad wombs.
verses.angle: Purusha experiences qualities born of nature
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: If nature creates the body, who is the one that actually experiences it? This verse answers that.

body.text: The inner being, situated in nature, experiences the qualities born of nature. Attachment to those qualities causes birth in good and bad wombs. The inner being, Purusha, sits inside nature and tastes its qualities. That same attachment to these qualities becomes the cause of being born into good or bad bodies. Krishna then describes how this inner self relates to the body as the witness, the giver of consent, and the great lord.

verses.sa: उपद्रष्टाऽनुमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः । परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन्पुरुषः परः ॥
verses.tr: The inner self becomes the witness, consent-giver, supporter, enjoyer, and great lord through its relation with the body. Yet in its true nature, it is called the supreme self and remains beyond the body.
verses.angle: The self's five apparent roles through the body
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now lists the roles the inner self seems to play. Listen for the chain of identities it takes on.

body.text: The inner self becomes the witness, consent-giver, supporter, enjoyer, and great lord through its relation with the body. Yet in its true nature, it is called the supreme self and remains beyond the body. The self seems to become five things, upadrashta, anumanta, bharta, bhokta, and maheshvara, yet in its true nature it is called the supreme self and remains beyond. Knowing this distinction between the self and the body frees one from rebirth.

verses.sa: य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैःसह । सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि न स भूयोऽभिजायते ॥
verses.tr: Whoever thus knows the purusha and prakriti together with the qualities is not born again, even while living and acting in every way.
verses.angle: Veitti: the knowing that ends rebirth
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna points to the moment of seeing itself. Listen for the single word that tells you how a person can act fully in the world and still break the cycle of birth.

body.text: Whoever thus knows the purusha and prakriti together with the qualities is not born again, even while living and acting in every way. The crucial word is veitti, knows. It is a clear knowing of the self, nature, and qualities. That knowing alone is what stops the cycle of rebirth. Krishna next names the three paths that lead a person to this knowing.

verses.sa: ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना । अन्ये सांख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे ॥
verses.tr: Some realize the true self within through meditation on the self. Others through clear discernment and yoga, and still others through the yoga of action.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described how a person who truly knows the self and the body is freed from birth. Now he explains how that knowing happens.

body.text: Some realize the true self within through meditation on the self. Others through clear discernment and yoga, and still others through the yoga of action. Krishna names three kinds of people: some, others, and yet others. He shows that the self is not reached by a single path alone. He then adds that even those who do not know these paths can cross beyond death if they listen to the teaching.

verses.sa: अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वाऽन्येभ्य उपासते । तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः ॥
verses.tr: Others do not know these paths, but they worship by hearing from others. Even they cross beyond death if they listen with devotion.
verses.angle: The path of listening and worship
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Not everyone can follow the hard paths of yoga directly, so Krishna speaks of a simpler way.

body.text: Others do not know these paths, but they worship by hearing from others. Even they cross beyond death if they listen with devotion. Krishna says even those who do not know the paths cross beyond death, because they listen with devotion to others who do. He now asks Arjuna to know the source of every moving and unmoving thing.

verses.tr: O best among the Bharatas, know that whatever comes into being, moving or unmoving, arises from the union of the field and the knower of the field.
verses.angle: Mamakah: the word that splits a family
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: The Gita opens far from the fighting, in a palace, where a blind king waits for news. Listen to how he names the two armies.

body.text: O best among the Bharatas, know that whatever comes into being, moving or unmoving, arises from the union of the field and the knower of the field. Listen again to one word, mamakah, my own. The Pandavas are his brother's sons, raised in his own house, and with that one word he splits the family into mine and theirs. Sanjaya answers with the king's own son, Duryodhana, looking across at the Pandava army.

verses.sa: समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम् । विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥
verses.tr: One who sees the supreme being equally present in all beings, imperishable amid the perishing, truly sees.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna shifts the lesson from the battlefield to the nature of reality, and asks Arjuna to look past the dying bodies to the one presence within them.

body.text: One who sees the supreme being equally present in all beings, imperishable amid the perishing, truly sees. The word avinashyantam means imperishable, and Krishna sets it against vinashyatsu, the perishing. He says the supreme being is unperishing among the perishing, and the one who sees this truly sees. Seeing the divine equally everywhere, a person does not wound the true self by the true self, and reaches the highest state.

verses.sa: समं पश्यन्हि सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम् । न हिनस्त्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
verses.tr: Seeing the divine equally everywhere, a person does not wound the true self by the true self, and reaches the highest state.
verses.angle: Hinasati: the self stops striking itself
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Listen for the word that makes the self stop wounding itself. Notice how Krishna connects seeing the divine with a person's final destination.

body.text: Seeing the divine equally everywhere, a person does not wound the true self by the true self, and reaches the highest state. The key word is hinasati, hurts, which literally means to strike or wound. A person who sees the divine equally everywhere stops striking the true self by the true self, and therefore goes to the highest state. Krishna then explains that the true self is the non-doer, while all actions are performed by nature alone.

prev.title: The field and the one who knows it
